title: SQL and Relational Databases
description: Queries, joins, keys, transactions and database design. 20 questions across all question types.

questions.prompt: Which SQL statement reads data from a table?
questions.explanation: SELECT queries data; the others change data or permissions.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters individual rows BEFORE they are grouped?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.prompt: Which clause filters groups AFTER aggregation?
questions.explanation: e.g. GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) > 5.

questions.prompt: A primary key column must be...
questions.explanation: A primary key identifies each row, so it can't repeat or be missing.

questions.prompt: Which join returns only the rows that match in both tables?
questions.explanation: Outer joins also keep unmatched rows; a cross join pairs every row with every row.

questions.prompt: What does COUNT(*) return?
options: The number of non-null values in the first column
questions.explanation: COUNT(*) counts rows; COUNT(column) skips nulls in that column.

questions.prompt: Which keyword removes duplicate rows from a query result?
questions.explanation: SELECT DISTINCT returns each combination of values once.

questions.prompt: A foreign key...
options: References a key in another (or the same) table
questions.explanation: Foreign keys enforce relationships (referential integrity) between tables.

questions.prompt: Which of these are aggregate functions?
questions.explanation: Aggregates combine many rows into one value; UPPER works on a single value.

questions.prompt: Which statements are DML (data manipulation)?
questions.explanation: CREATE TABLE is DDL: it defines structure rather than changing data.

questions.prompt: Which properties make up ACID?
questions.explanation: Availability belongs to the CAP theorem, not ACID.

questions.prompt: In SQL, NULL = NULL evaluates to TRUE.
questions.explanation: Comparisons with NULL are unknown; use IS NULL instead.

questions.prompt: An index can speed up reads but slow down writes.
questions.explanation: Every insert or update must also maintain the index.

questions.prompt: ORDER BY sorts in ascending order unless told otherwise.
questions.explanation: ASC is the default; add DESC for descending.

questions.prompt: To add new rows to a table you use the ___ INTO statement.
questions.explanation: INSERT INTO table (columns) VALUES (...).

questions.prompt: A LEFT JOIN keeps every row from the ___ table, even without a match.
questions.explanation: Unmatched rows get NULLs for the right table's columns.

questions.prompt: Table A has 3 rows and table B has 4 rows. How many rows does A CROSS JOIN B return?
questions.explanation: A cross join pairs every row of A with every row of B: 3 × 4 = 12.

questions.prompt: Put the logical processing order of a SELECT query in order.
questions.explanation: That's why a column alias defined in SELECT can be used in ORDER BY but not in WHERE.

questions.prompt: Order these normal forms from weakest to strongest.
questions.explanation: Each normal form builds on the previous one to remove more redundancy.

questions.prompt: Match each command with its purpose.

pairs.right: Define a new table or object
Remove a table or object entirely
Quickly delete all rows from a table

questions.explanation: These are DDL commands that work on structure rather than individual rows.
